column1: # Devices that need more power to charge at full speed than an ordinary USB port gives, read by PowerNeeds.cs.
# Each line is one device: tab-separated vendor ID, product ID, product string, watts, name, basis and source.
#   vendor     Four hex digits, as USB Atlas shows VID:PID.
#   product    Four hex digits, or * when the maker changes the product ID with what the device is doing, as a
#              headset's changes between file sharing, Link and developer modes.
#   string     The product string the device reports, or * for any.
#   watts      What it needs to charge at full speed.
#   name       What it is, in our own words.
#   basis      Where the figure comes from, in a phrase that reads after the name and figure.
#   source     The maker's page the figure is taken from.
# Sourcing: every figure is the maker's own, from its own support or product pages; reviews, forums and resale
# listings aren't used. Only devices that need more than a 5 V port can give (15 W), or close to it, are worth
# listing. Quest 3 reports the product string "Quest 3" (seen on hardware, as 2833:5010 in Link and 2833:5011 with
# file sharing on); "Quest 2" is what Quest 2 reports in lsusb output quoted in libmtp's issue tracker. The Quest 3S
# and Quest Pro strings are Meta's product names, not yet seen on hardware.
